title: Order-Robustness Audit of Gradient Masking Methods for Continual Learning in LLMs

contributions.purpose: Test whether the published ranking of gradient masking methods holds under a different task ordering.
contributions.mechanism: Audit FGGM (Fisher-guided task-level masking) and MIGU (magnitude-based batch-level masking) plus an SFT baseline on TRACE under an alternative Order 2 that front-loads numerical reasoning tasks (Qwen2-1.5B).
contributions.evaluation: Ranking reversal: MIGU outperforms FGGM by 2.95 TRACE-OP points on Order 2 (43.72 vs 40.77), reversing FGGM's reported default-order advantage; FGGM underperforms MIGU in all 3 seeds.
contributions.domain: Continual learning for LLMs (gradient masking, TRACE benchmark)
contributions.source_quote: we demonstrate that FGGM's advantage over MIGU on TRACE is order-specific: MIGU outperforms FGGM by 2.95 TRACE-OP points on Order 2, reversing the published ranking.

contributions.purpose: Quantify each method's robustness to task ordering.
contributions.mechanism: Define Order Sensitivity as the TRACE-OP drop from default order to Order 2 and compare drops and BWT across methods.
contributions.evaluation: MIGU shows the smallest drop (3.71 points) vs FGGM (5.07) and SFT (9.49); MIGU also best BWT on Order 2 (-1.07 vs FGGM -3.41, SFT -5.30).
contributions.source_quote: we show that MIGU exhibits superior order-robustness, with only a 3.71-point TRACE-OP drop from default to Order 2, compared to FGGM's 5.07-point drop.

contributions.purpose: Explain the mechanism behind FGGM's order sensitivity.
contributions.mechanism: Analyze consecutive task-pair Jaccard similarity of FGGM's binary masks under both orderings, identifying a low-overlap disruption mechanism.
contributions.evaluation: Order 2's early NumGLUE-cm->NumGLUE-ds transition has lowest Jaccard (0.368) with monotonic increase (0.300->0.589), vs moderate default-order overlap (0.527-0.587), causing disruptive early parameter shifts.
contributions.domain: Mechanistic analysis of task-level gradient masking
contributions.source_quote: we identify a 'low-overlap disruption' mechanism explaining FGGM's order sensitivity: Order 2's front-loaded numerical reasoning tasks produce atypical Fisher patterns with low consecutive mask overlap, causing disruptive early parameter shifts.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our audit compares FGGM (Tan et al., 2026) and MIGU (Du et al., 2024) against a sequential fine-tuning (SFT) baseline on the TRACE benchmark (Wang et al., 2023b) under two task orderings.
We use Qwen2-1.5B (Yang et al., 2024) as the base model, following the FGGM paper's experimental setup.
Task ordering significantly affects continual learning performance (Bell & Lawrence, 2022), with different sequences producing varying degrees of catastrophic forgetting.
APD-Net (Yoon et al., 2019) explicitly addresses order-robustness through additive parameter decomposition.

notes: Reproduction caveat reported as a failed sanity check: authors' MIGU deviates +3.35 TRACE-OP from published (exceeds +/-2.0 tolerance) due to gradient-interception implementation differences; they argue the Order 2 comparison remains valid since both orderings use their identical MIGU. Mechanistic analysis acknowledged as correlational, and only one alternative ordering tested.
